title: Design
description: The canonical production design, two-faced: a declared standard and one visual language a designer signs; per-screen structure, states and controls Delivery binds to. One design per screen the backlog claims, nothing else. The writer declares the standard it will be held to — a direction, the hero moments, its commitments — then composes the tokens, the stylesheet, the screens, notes and open questions; the runner owns identity, traces, the hash and the sign-off.

traces.description: What this design was written from. Any hash moving makes the design stale — the badge, not a block.

standard.description: The standard you declare and are then held to. The reviewer judges the screens against this and against the craft floor; it does not judge whether it would have chosen it.

direction.description: The point of view, in a sentence with nouns from this product's world, and why it serves the people in the PRD. Not a synonym pile; not something that could be pasted onto another product unchanged.

heroes.description: The two or three moments where the design earns its keep — each on a screen this design holds, with what is on screen at that moment. The system's strongest treatment is spent here and nowhere else.

commitments.description: What the design promises and can be checked against: the type families and weights, the space unit, the neutrals' temperature, how separation is earned, what status never relies on. Each is a line the reviewer holds every screen to.

tokens.description: The visual language as named decisions — palette, type scale and ratio, space unit, radii, touch-target minimum, status treatments. Every screen renders from these and nothing else.

stylesheet.description: Shippable production CSS realizing the tokens as custom properties, with focus-visible and pressed states, and motion that is absent under reduced-motion. A build that adopts it verbatim looks designed.

screens.description: One per screen the backlog claims, keyed by the prototype's screen id. Nothing else.

moment.description: Where and how this screen is read — the surface, the distance, the hands, the light — and the density that calls for.

structure.description: The semantic outline — elements, roles, order, data slots, final microcopy — specific enough that two implementers produce the same DOM shape.

states.description: Every state the screen renders — initial, populated, empty, faulted — and what each shows and withholds. Together they partition the screen's life.

renders.description: What a person sees in this state and not in the others, testably.

entered_by.description: What brings the screen into this state, when it is not the initial one.

controls.description: Every control the structure names, with a stable id downstream cites. Mint once; keep the same id for the same control across rewrites.

kind.description: button, link, field, chip, toggle, list, …

label.description: The final string a person reads, in the product's vocabulary.

state.description: The state this control appears in, when it is not every state.

notes.description: For the PM and the designer who signs: where the prototype was kept and where it was left, what the surface forced, what was hard.

open_questions.description: What designing exposed that the PRD and the backlog do not answer — as questions for the PM, never as decisions taken in pixels.

subject.description: The SCREEN, STORY or REQ it concerns, if one.

blocking.description: True if the screen cannot be designed sensibly until this is answered.

signoff.description: A named human designer's word on this exact design, beside the reviewer's verdict at the time. Outside the hash: signing does not change the design; regenerating makes the signature stale.

override.description: Present only when a blocking review was overridden — a human's word, on the record.

x-drift-checked.description: The pointers the content hash covers: the standard, the tokens, the stylesheet and the screens.
